subject: Follow-up: hosting risk scope, evidence needed & next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Connor Li <connor.li@medsure.io>, MedSure Security <security@medsure.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: hosting risk scope, evidence needed & next steps

Connor / MedSure team — thanks again for the conversation this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we can align on the hosting path (Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC) and the security evidence you'll need for procurement.

Recap (key constraints you shared):
- Primary requirement: PHI processing for clinical triage -> prefer an environment with contractual safeguards (BAA) and at-rest/data-in-transit controls.
- SOC 2 evidence will be required for the procurement packet; auditor period needs callout.
- You have an upcoming vendor security review on 12/15; ideally we deliver initial evidence and BAA draft before then.

Redwood recommendations (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest to integrate; acceptable only if MedSure will de-identify PHI before sending.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs): good balance — physical isolation of customer workloads, single-tenant pool, Redwood-managed infra; supports BAA and SOC2 evidence with limited operational customization.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): required if MedSure cannot de-identify PHI or needs full network control and on-prem audit constraints.

Evidence we plan to provide by 12/08:
1) SOC 2 summary and scope + auditor name (redwood_soc2_summary.pdf)
2) Draft BAA for your legal review (BAA_draft_20271205.docx)
3) High-level inference architecture diagram showing network boundaries and data flows (inference_arch_diagram.png)
4) Completed vendor questionnaire template (we ask you to share your questionnaire; below is a suggested mapping)

Open items / asks for MedSure:
- Please confirm whether you will be sending PHI in identifiable form or using de-id before sending.
- Share your vendor security questionnaire (spreadsheet or doc) so we can pre-populate answers.
- Confirm the SOC 2 report period and any specific control requirements (e.g., encryption algorithms, KMS/HSM expectations).

Next steps / timeline:
- 12/05: I’ll send the SOC2 summary, draft BAA, and architecture diagram (attached).
- 12/06–12/08: Redwood to map your questionnaire and return a filled copy.
- 12/09: follow-up technical call (30m) to review dedicated/private deployment checklist — propose 10:00 AM PT.

Attachments: postcall_notes_20271205.pdf (internal notes), redwood_soc2_summary.pdf (planned), BAA_draft_20271205.docx (planned), inference_arch_diagram.png (planned)

Thanks — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Karthik — good notes. Couple quick clarifications and I attached our standard security questionnaire so you can map answers.

Questions:
1) For Dedicated capacity, will Redwood provide customer-specific VPC peering or do you rely on private networking within Redwood-managed fabric? We need peering for our logging pipeline.
2) What is your default retention for inference logs and how configurable is that per-customer (we'd like 90 days, with option to extend)?
3) If we choose Hosted API with de-id, do you provide guidance / tooling for typical de-identification patterns?

Attached: MedSure_Security_Questionnaire.csv (filled by our security team)

Date: Tue, 06 Dec 2027 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: hosting risk scope, evidence needed & next steps

Connor — thanks for the questions and for sending the questionnaire. Answers inline below, and I’ve attached the files we referenced.

Answers (high level):
1) Dedicated capacity networking: Redwood supports VPC peering for Dedicated deployments in major clouds; for Dedicated we can either do VPC peering or an AWS Transit/PrivateLink pattern depending on your preference and compliance needs. We will map logging endpoints and can provide an agent or forwarder spec for your pipeline.

2) Inference logs retention: default is 30 days; configurable up to 365 days depending on plan and storage tier. For Dedicated and Private customers we can keep 90 days by default and extend via a retention policy (costs apply). We can surface token-level logs or aggregated metrics per your request.

3) Hosted de-identification guidance: yes — Redwood provides a de-id reference doc and a lightweight SDK helper that strips common PHI fields before submission. We’ll share patterns and examples (PHI redaction vs tokenization tradeoffs). Note: de-id is not a substitute for contractual requirements if your internal policy disallows sending identifiers off-prem.

Attachments included: MedSure_Security_Questionnaire_filled_mapping.csv (mapping from your questionnaire to Redwood evidence), redwood_soc2_summary.pdf, inference_arch_diagram.png

Proposed next steps (revised):
- 12/08: Redwood returns mapped questionnaire and initial evidence docs.
- 12/09: 10:00 AM PT technical call to review Dedicated vs Private checklist. Please confirm availability.
- 12/12: Legal leads to exchange BAA redlines (BAA_draft_20271205.docx will be sent).

If you confirm that de-id is acceptable, we can also propose a short pilot on Hosted (no PHI) to validate latency and cost before committing to Dedicated.

Best — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fwd: Follow-up: hosting risk scope, evidence needed & next steps

Forwarding with a couple of legal / contract notes. Connor — looping in our legal counsel (we can provide actual person once scope is agreed). A few asks from legal/security side to help speed review: 

1) SOC 2 report specifics we need: report period (last 12 months rolling), evidence of controls around encryption-in-transit and at-rest, key-management practices (KMS/HSM), and evidence of employee background checks for ops team.
2) Please confirm if MedSure requires subprocessor disclosures and whether your procurement team expects a named-subprocessor list in the BAA.
3) For the BAA draft: we prefer to receive single consolidated redlines (not multiple versions) and will respond within 3 business days once received.

Attaching BAA draft for MedSure review: BAA_draft_20271205.docx

Marissa Cole
Director, GTM Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
